intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Arrive early to catch the freshest produce and interact with vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a hefty price tag. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 morning to kick off your culinary journey refreshed.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's legendary electric town, Akihabara, packed with multi-floor electronics stores, retro arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget shops. Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller indie shops for the latest tech. Ideal for afternoons when shops are fully stocked and buzzing with energy. Staying in nearby Asakusa or Ueno keeps you within a short train ride, maximizing your time here.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. The area comes alive in the early morning before crowds arrive, offering a serene cultural experience. Staying in Asakusa puts you steps away, making this a perfect early morning activity even on Day 2 after your late Day 1 arrival.

experiences.name: Shibuya Crossing and Izakaya Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening hours, then wind down with a traditional izakaya dinner nearby, sampling yakitori, edamame, and Japanese whisky. The Shibuya and Shinjuku corridor is a central hub, and choosing a hotel in this area eliminates long commutes. This experience blends iconic Tokyo culture with authentic local dining in one evening outing.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, a cutting-edge digital art museum blending technology and culture through interactive, boundary-dissolving installations. This experience perfectly bridges Tokyo's tech culture and artistic heritage. Book tickets in advance online to save time. The Azabudai Hills location is accessible from central Tokyo hotels in Shibuya or Roppongi, keeping travel time minimal.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to central Tokyo and check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed stroll around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (free entry) to shake off jet lag and soak in the surroundings near your hotel. Walk along the moat and enjoy the spring scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Akihabara Electric Town (15-min walk/short metro from Chiyoda) – window-shop electronics, retro game shops, and anime culture. Get a feel for Tokyo's famous tech district.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, affordable set meal at a convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) near the airport or station – onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods for under ¥600.
meals.dinner: Eat at a local ramen shop in Akihabara – try Ichiran or a local tonkotsu spot for around ¥800–¥1,200 per bowl.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport or station for seamless travel on trains and buses throughout the trip. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,000 for transport from airport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (free entry) – arrive early to beat crowds, walk Nakamise Shopping Street, and browse traditional crafts and snacks. Try ningyo-yaki (small cakes) for ¥200–¥300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno Park (free) and explore the Ueno area. Visit the Tokyo National Museum if interested in Japanese history and culture (¥1,000 entry). Walk through Ameyoko Market for street food and bargain shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Akihabara for a deeper dive into tech culture – visit multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and explore retro game arcades.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near your hotel – coffee, onigiri, or tamagoyaki sandwich for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Street food at Ameyoko Market – grilled seafood skewers, takoyaki, or yakitori for ¥500–¥800.
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya in Akihabara – filling and delicious for ¥500–¥700.

day_by_day.notes: Asakusa is about 20–25 minutes by metro from Chiyoda. Purchase a day pass (¥600) if you plan multiple metro rides.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku – visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free) set in a serene forested area. A peaceful contrast to the city buzz.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street to experience Tokyo's quirky youth fashion culture, then head to Omotesando for window shopping and people-watching (budget-friendly – no need to buy anything).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya – experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing. Visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Sky or the free Mag's Park rooftop for a city view.

meals.breakfast: Grab a morning set at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) near Chiyoda – toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Crepes on Takeshita Street (¥400–¥600) or a quick kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) lunch for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Shibuya food hall (depachika) basement of Shibuya Hikarie or Tokyu Food Show – pick up bento boxes, sushi sets, and sides for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is a 5-min walk from Harajuku Station. Shibuya Scramble is best experienced at dusk when the lights come on – very atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market (free to walk) – sample fresh tamagoyaki, sushi rolls, and seafood snacks from street stalls. A must for food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ginza (15 min from Tsukiji) – explore Japan's upscale shopping district. Window-shop flagship stores and visit the free Itoya stationery store. Check out the free Ginza Six rooftop garden.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back toward Chiyoda and explore the Nihonbashi area – a historic commercial district with beautiful bridges and architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast – fresh sushi, tamagoyaki on a stick, and grilled scallops for ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Soba or udon at a local noodle shop in Ginza's backstreets – look for lunch specials for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Try a standing sushi bar (tachinomi/tachigui sushi) near Nihonbashi for fresh, affordable sushi – ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most lively in the morning. Saturday crowds can be large – arrive by 9:00 AM for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shinjuku – visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) for a beautiful green escape in the city, especially lovely in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's famous Golden Gai district (a maze of tiny bars and restaurants) and Kabukicho entertainment district. Browse the massive Yodobashi Akiba tech store or Bic Camera.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck in Shinjuku (open until 23:00 on some nights) for a stunning panoramic night view of Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or bakery near Chiyoda – melon pan or curry bread with coffee for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Katsu curry at CoCo Ichibanya in Shinjuku – customizable and filling for ¥800–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Ramen at Fuunji (tsukemen specialist) or a local izakaya in Shinjuku – budget ¥900–¥1,500 for ramen or a small izakaya set.

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free and offers one of the best city views without spending on paid observatories. Check opening hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Yanaka – one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Explore Yanaka Cemetery, Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and traditional temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nezu Shrine (free) with its beautiful torii gate tunnels, then walk to Yanesen area (Yanaka, Nezu, Sendagi) for artisan shops and local cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chiyoda and visit the area around Kanda – explore Jimbocho, Tokyo's famous book town, with hundreds of second-hand and specialty bookshops.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your hotel or a nearby convenience store.
meals.lunch: Street food at Yanaka Ginza – try menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) or croquettes for ¥200–¥400 each.
meals.dinner: Kanda local izakaya – order a few small plates (yakitori, edamame, tofu) and a drink for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is about 20 minutes from Chiyoda by metro (Chiyoda Line to Nezu or Nishi-Nippori). This area offers an authentic old Tokyo atmosphere rarely seen by tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba – take the futuristic Yurikamome monorail (scenic ride) to this man-made island. See the life-size Gundam statue (free) and the teamLab digital art complex exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free mall), visit the free Fuji TV building exterior and Odaiba Seaside Park for views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Head back and explore the Marunouchi/Tokyo Station area near Chiyoda – beautifully lit at night. Browse the Tokyo Character Street underground mall (free to browse).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast before heading out.
meals.lunch: Food court at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza – various Japanese options for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Tokyo Station's underground Ramen Street – choose from 8 famous ramen shops for ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless or Planets requires advance booking and costs ¥3,200–¥3,800 – skip if strictly budget-conscious or book if it's a priority. The Yurikamome monorail costs about ¥400 one way.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Akihabara in depth – visit the Radio Kaikan building for electronics components and retro tech, explore multi-floor maid cafes (budget ¥500–¥1,000 for a coffee and experience), and browse doujinshi (indie manga) shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the 2k540 Aki-Oka Artisan market under the JR train tracks between Akihabara and Okachimachi – unique crafts and artisan workshops in a cool industrial setting.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji – a bohemian neighborhood known for vintage clothing, live music venues, and indie culture. Walk around the covered shopping arcades.

meals.breakfast: Akihabara convenience store or a local kissaten for a morning set ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Curry at a local Indian-Japanese fusion spot in Akihabara for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Koenji local izakaya or a small family-run restaurant – try teishoku (set meal) for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Koenji is about 25 minutes by JR Chuo Line from Akihabara. This is a great area to experience local Tokyo nightlife without the tourist premium.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ikebukuro – explore the massive Sunshine City complex, the free Sunshine Aquarium exterior, and the otaku culture hub of Animate (anime merchandise store).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free observation floor at Sunshine 60 (or budget for the paid deck at ¥700) and explore the Nishiikebukuro Park area. Browse the Tokyu Hands lifestyle store for unique Japanese products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chiyoda and visit the Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) – one of Tokyo's oldest shrines, beautifully illuminated at night and closely connected to tech and gaming culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store breakfast.
meals.lunch: Sunshine City food court – wide variety of affordable Japanese food for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Yakitori alley near Yurakucho (close to Chiyoda) – charcoal-grilled skewers under the train tracks for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Myojin is particularly beloved by tech and gaming communities – you'll often see ema (wishing plaques) dedicated to computers and game characters.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kamakura (about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line) – visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300 entry) and surrounding temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills, visit Hasedera Temple (¥400) with ocean views, and explore Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo and relax near the hotel. Pick up dinner from a depachika or supermarket for a budget-friendly evening.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl or seafood at a local Kamakura restaurant for ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Supermarket bento or sushi from a nearby Seiyu or Maruetsu supermarket near Chiyoda for ¥600–¥900.

day_by_day.notes: JR Pass holders can use it for this trip. Without a pass, round-trip from Tokyo to Kamakura is about ¥1,940. Buy the Kamakura-Enoshima Pass (¥700) for unlimited local train rides within Kamakura.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) – a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, surrounded by modern skyscrapers. Take the water bus from here to Asakusa (¥800 – scenic river cruise).
day_by_day.afternoon: Back in Asakusa, explore the backstreets and the Kappabashi Kitchen Town – a fascinating street of wholesale restaurant supply shops selling kitchenware, plastic food models, and chef tools.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nakameguro area – walk along the canal (beautiful with cherry blossoms or greenery in April) lined with independent boutiques, cafes, and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten breakfast near Chiyoda – morning set with toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Monja-yaki (Tokyo's own savory pancake) in Asakusa or Tsukishima – hands-on cooking at the table for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal-side cafe or a budget ramen/noodle shop in the area for ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: The Hamarikyu to Asakusa water bus is a unique and scenic way to see Tokyo from the water. Runs every 40–60 minutes – check the schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (¥600 entry) – an incredible museum covering 400 years of Tokyo's history with life-size reconstructions. Highly recommended for culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ryogoku – the sumo district. Visit the Kokugikan Sumo Arena exterior and the free Sumo Museum inside (check schedule for tournaments). Walk around the chanko-nabe restaurant district.
day_by_day.evening: Final exploration of Akihabara for any last-minute tech or culture shopping. Visit a multi-floor arcade (Round One or Taito Station) for a fun evening of Japanese arcade games.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Chanko-nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew) at a local restaurant in Ryogoku – hearty and affordable at ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Akihabara – try a Japanese curry chain (Coco Ichibanya) or a cheap sushi conveyor belt for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: The Edo-Tokyo Museum may have temporary exhibitions with additional fees. Check for any special exhibitions before visiting. Sumo tournaments happen in January, May, and September in Tokyo – April is between tournaments but the museum is still open.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – visit the Imperial Palace East Gardens one more time or stroll through Kitanomaru Park (free) adjacent to the palace for a peaceful farewell to Tokyo. Visit the Science Museum (Kagaku Gijutsukan) if open for a tech-culture finale (¥830).
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack, check out of the hotel, and store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at Tokyo Station. Do final souvenir shopping at Tokyo Character Street or the Marunouchi Building shops near Tokyo Station.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport (Narita or Haneda) with plenty of time. Enjoy one last convenience store meal or a quick soba at a station noodle shop before departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese convenience store breakfast – a ritual worth repeating. Try a different onigiri flavor and a hot canned coffee for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Ekiben (train station bento box) from Tokyo Station's extensive selection – beautifully packaged regional bento for ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Airport or station soba/udon – a classic, affordable last meal in Japan for ¥600–¥900.

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers at Tokyo Station are available in various sizes (¥300–¥700 for several hours). Allow at least 90 minutes to reach Narita Airport from central Tokyo, or 45 minutes to Haneda. Validate your Suica card balance can be refunded at any JR station before departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City (~60-90 min). Check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen) — free entry, stunning moat views, and peaceful greenery perfect for shaking off jet lag. Explore the nearby Kitanomaru Park area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Jinbocho, Chiyoda's famous book-town neighborhood. Browse quirky secondhand bookshops and soak in the local intellectual atmosphere as shops wind down for the evening.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick set meal (teishoku) at a casual restaurant near Tokyo Station upon arrival — try Yodobashi or Gransta food hall inside Tokyo Station for affordable ramen or soba (~¥900-1,200)
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba (老舗) near Jinbocho — a historic soba restaurant serving handmade buckwheat noodles in a traditional setting (~¥1,500-2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul travel. Avoid over-scheduling. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April weather is typically mild (15-20°C) with possible cherry blossom remnants.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukiji Outer Market (15 min by subway from Chiyoda) for a classic Tokyo food experience. Explore fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki vendors, and specialty food shops. Arrive by 8:30 AM for the best selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara Electric Town (10 min walk or short subway from hotel) — Tokyo's iconic tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics stores (Yodobashi Akiba, BIC Camera), retro game shops, and anime merchandise stores. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center for vintage electronics culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the vibrant neon-lit streets after dark. Pop into a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience, or visit Super Potato retro game shop before it closes at 8 PM.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh uni (sea urchin) on rice, grilled scallops, or a classic tamago sushi set from a market stall (~¥800-1,500)
meals.lunch: Ramen at Fuunji or a local Akihabara ramen shop — try tsukemen (dipping ramen) (~¥1,000-1,300)
meals.dinner: Yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) at a mid-range restaurant in Akihabara — enjoy grilling your own wagyu cuts at the table (~¥2,500-3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is extremely walkable and best explored on foot. Most electronics and game shops open around 10-11 AM. The area is lively until 9-10 PM. Bring a small bag for purchases — it's easy to overspend on gadgets and collectibles!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (20 min by subway) — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive early (by 8 AM) to beat crowds. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks and crafts. Climb the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, visit the historic cemetery, and browse independent craft shops and galleries. This area offers a rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno Park area for the evening. Visit Ameyoko Market street for lively bargain shopping and street food. The area transforms into a buzzing local food and drink scene after work hours.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a small kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Senso-ji for morning coffee and toast set (~¥600-900)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food lunch — try menchi-katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet) from a local butcher stall and fresh cream puffs (~¥500-800 total)
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Ueno — join salary workers for yakitori skewers, edamame, and cold draft beer at a lively standing bar or sit-down izakaya (~¥2,000-3,000 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, but the inner hall has specific hours. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Ameyoko Market is busiest on weekday evenings and weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets TOKYO in Toyosu (30 min by subway) — an immersive digital art museum featuring stunning light and water installations. Book tickets in advance online. Opens at 9 AM on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba, the futuristic man-made island in Tokyo Bay. Visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue), stroll the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge, and browse the unique architecture of the area.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Venus Fort (or its successor retail area) and the Palette Town area for evening shopping and dining. Enjoy the bay views illuminated at night from the Odaiba seaside park.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store morning — 7-Eleven or FamilyMart onigiri, egg sandwich, and canned coffee (~¥400-600) — a genuine local experience
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Toyosu Market's restaurant floor (adjacent to teamLab) — fresh sushi or seafood donburi bowls (~¥1,800-2,800)
meals.dinner: Odaiba dining — try a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Sushi Zanmai or a casual tonkatsu restaurant with bay views (~¥1,500-2,500)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets MUST be booked in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Wear or bring socks as parts of the exhibit require removing shoes. Odaiba is connected by the Yurikamome automated monorail — the ride itself offers great views of the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku — visit Takeshita Street for youth fashion culture, cosplay shops, and crepe stands. Then walk through the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) surrounded by a forested sanctuary in the middle of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's most elegant tree-lined boulevard. Browse the architecturally stunning brand flagships and boutiques. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex designed by Tadao Ando. Explore the hidden Ura-Harajuku backstreets for independent designers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing scramble experience at peak evening hour. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck on top of Scramble Square for 360° city views (book in advance). Explore the Shibuya Stream and PARCO areas.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or Angelica on Takeshita Street — a classic Tokyo sweet treat (~¥500-700)
meals.lunch: Omotesando lunch at a café or brasserie — try the underground Omotesando Hills B2 food area or a Japanese curry restaurant (~¥1,200-1,800)
meals.dinner: Shibuya dining — visit Nonbei Yokocho ('Drunkard's Alley') for tiny atmospheric bars and small plates, or try a modern izakaya in Shibuya STREAM (~¥2,500-3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free but the inner treasury has a small fee. Sunday mornings at Yoyogi Park (adjacent to Meiji Jingu) often feature street performers and local gatherings — worth a peek. Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic on weekend evenings when foot traffic peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science and the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park (both open by 9:30 AM). The Tokyo National Museum houses the world's largest collection of Japanese art and artifacts — allow 2-3 hours. Combined entry ~¥1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akihabara's tech culture deeper — visit the Akihabara UDX tech hub, explore the Kotobukiya hobby store, and check out the SEGA and Taito Station game centers for a uniquely Japanese gaming culture experience. Try crane games and rhythm arcade games.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Kanda Myojin Shrine — one of Tokyo's oldest shrines, famously associated with IT and tech companies (many game companies hold blessing ceremonies here). Then explore the atmospheric Kanda area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Ueno Seiyoken Grill or a bakery café near Ueno Park — try a morning set with coffee and pastry (~¥700-1,000)
meals.lunch: Museum café lunch inside Tokyo National Museum or a nearby restaurant in Ueno — try a traditional Japanese bento set (~¥1,200-1,600)
meals.dinner: Kanda area dinner — try Kanda Matsuya for handmade soba noodles in a historic building (open since 1884), a true Tokyo institution (~¥1,200-2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays — check the schedule and substitute with the National Museum of Western Art or Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum if needed. Kanda Myojin is particularly interesting for its connection to Japanese tech culture — look for ema (wooden wishing plaques) decorated with anime and game characters.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko (2 hours by Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa, ~¥1,400 each way) — a UNESCO World Heritage mountain town with ornate Edo-period shrines and temples. Visit Toshogu Shrine complex with its famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys carving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the photogenic Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls (one of Japan's most famous waterfalls).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (~6-7 PM). Rest at the hotel or take a quiet evening walk around the Imperial Palace moat, beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or convenience store before catching the train from Asakusa (~¥400-600)
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty. Try a yuba kaiseki set lunch at a restaurant near Toshogu Shrine (~¥1,500-2,500)
meals.dinner: Light dinner near the hotel — try a neighborhood ramen shop or Japanese curry restaurant in Chiyoda (~¥900-1,400)

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (by 8 AM) to maximize time in Nikko. The Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (~¥4,000) covers round-trip train and local buses and is worth the investment. Nikko's mountain weather can be cooler than Tokyo — bring a light jacket. Toshogu Shrine entry is ¥1,300.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum and Tokyo City View observation deck in Roppongi Hills (opens 10 AM). The museum features cutting-edge contemporary art exhibitions, and the observation deck offers spectacular 360° views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art district — visit the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Tokyo Midtown (designed by Tadao Ando, dedicated to design culture) and browse the Suntory Museum of Art. The Roppongi Art Triangle is one of Tokyo's most sophisticated cultural zones.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Roppongi's nightlife and dining scene — the area transforms dramatically after dark with international restaurants, jazz bars, and rooftop lounges. Visit Roppongi Hills Arena for any evening events or performances.

meals.breakfast: Azabu Juban neighborhood breakfast (a short walk from Roppongi) — try a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten (~¥700-1,000)
meals.lunch: Tokyo Midtown food hall lunch — excellent variety from Japanese to international cuisine at mid-range prices (~¥1,200-1,800)
meals.dinner: Roppongi dinner — try Gonpachi Nishiazabu (the inspiration for the Kill Bill restaurant scene) for izakaya-style Japanese food in a dramatic multi-story setting (~¥3,000-4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open late (until 10 PM on most days) making it perfect for evening visits too. The combined Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View ticket is ~¥2,000. Check the museum's current exhibition before visiting. Roppongi Hills and Tokyo Midtown are both excellent for architecture appreciation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (30 min by subway) — a fascinating large-scale museum documenting Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era. Excellent scale models and interactive exhibits. Opens at 9:30 AM (~¥600 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ryogoku, Tokyo's sumo district. Visit the Sumo Museum (free), walk around the Kokugikan sumo arena, and explore the neighborhood where sumo stables are located. If lucky, you may spot sumo wrestlers walking to practice in the morning hours.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa (30 min by train) for Tokyo's indie music and vintage culture scene. Browse vinyl record shops, vintage clothing stores, and small live music venues. These neighborhoods represent a completely different side of Tokyo from the tourist circuit.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Chiyoda neighborhood café morning set (~¥700-1,000)
meals.lunch: Chanko nabe (sumo wrestler's hot pot stew) at a Ryogoku chanko restaurant — a hearty, protein-rich meal in the sumo heartland (~¥1,500-2,500)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa dinner — try a small, character-filled curry restaurant or a natural wine bar with Japanese small plates (~¥2,000-3,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Edo-Tokyo Museum is one of the most informative museums in Tokyo for understanding the city's history — highly recommended. Sumo tournaments (basho) are held in January, May, and September at Kokugikan — April is between tournaments, but the neighborhood atmosphere remains. Shimokitazawa is best experienced in the evening when its café and bar scene comes alive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (if reopened at its new Azabudai Hills location) or the Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation in Odaiba. Miraikan features ASIMO robots, space exploration exhibits, and cutting-edge tech demonstrations — perfect for tech culture interest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shiodome and the Caretta Shiodome shopping complex. Visit the Advertising Museum Tokyo (AdMT) — a free, fascinating museum documenting Japanese advertising history and pop culture from the Edo period to today. Then walk along the Hamarikyu Gardens, a stunning traditional garden with a tidal pond.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ginza district for an upscale Tokyo evening. Window shop at the flagship stores on Chuo-dori, visit the Itoya stationery megastore, and explore the Ginza Six complex. Ginza is a 15-minute walk from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri, tamagoyaki, miso soup cup) eaten in Hamarikyu Gardens — a quintessential local Tokyo experience (~¥400-600)
meals.lunch: Tsukiji area lunch (a short walk from Hamarikyu) — fresh sushi set at an outer market restaurant (~¥1,500-2,500)
meals.dinner: Ginza dinner — try a mid-range sushi counter (omakase at lunch price level) or a tempura restaurant in Ginza's side streets (~¥3,000-4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entry is ¥300 and is one of Tokyo's most beautiful traditional gardens. The AdMT is free and surprisingly engaging even for non-advertising enthusiasts. Ginza on Friday evenings is vibrant — many galleries have late opening hours and the streets are lively with after-work crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station) — a coastal city with 65 Buddhist temples and 19 Shinto shrines. Start at the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu) — a 13-meter bronze statue dating to 1252. Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's temples — visit Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji Zen temples, then walk down the historic Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, matcha sweets, and handmade goods. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine, Kamakura's most important.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Spend the evening at Shinjuku — visit the Golden Gai (a labyrinth of tiny atmospheric bars), explore Kabukicho entertainment district, or relax at a rooftop bar with views of the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab breakfast at Tokyo Station's Gransta food hall before boarding (~¥600-900)
meals.lunch: Kamakura shirasu (baby sardines) rice bowl at a restaurant near Komachi-dori — a famous local specialty (~¥1,200-1,800)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Golden Gai dinner — hop between tiny bars, each with 6-8 seats and unique themes. Order small plates (tsumami) and drinks at 2-3 bars (~¥2,500-3,500 total)

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:30 AM from Tokyo Station. The Kamakura-Enoshima Pass (~¥1,500) covers round-trip travel and local trains. Kamakura is hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes. Golden Gai bars can be cash-only and some have cover charges (~¥500-1,000) — this is normal and part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo Skytree (20 min by subway from Chiyoda) — Tokyo's tallest structure at 634 meters. Book the Tembo Deck (350m) and Tembo Galleria (450m) tickets in advance. On a clear spring morning, views of Mt. Fuji and the entire Kanto Plain are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nakameguro and Daikanyama — Tokyo's most stylish residential neighborhoods. Walk along the Meguro River (lined with cafés and boutiques), visit the Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning bookstore and cultural complex), and browse the independent shops of Log Road Daikanyama.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out — return to Shibuya or explore the Ebisu/Daikanyama area for dinner. Visit a rooftop bar or spend the evening at a standing sushi bar for an authentic local dining experience. Reflect on the trip over a final Japanese whisky at a bar.

meals.breakfast: Skytree area — try a traditional Japanese breakfast at a restaurant in Solamachi (the Skytree's shopping complex) (~¥900-1,400)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro lunch — a trendy café lunch along the river canal. Many excellent brunch spots with Japanese-Western fusion menus (~¥1,200-1,800)
meals.dinner: Daikanyama or Ebisu restaurant dinner — try a modern Japanese restaurant or a quality yakitori counter for a celebratory last full-day dinner (~¥3,000-4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets should be booked online in advance, especially on weekends. Morning visits offer the best chance of clear views. Daikanyama T-Site is a must for book and culture lovers — it stocks an impressive selection of Japanese art, design, and travel books. The Meguro River walk is especially beautiful in April with late cherry blossoms possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take a peaceful early walk around the Imperial Palace moat (Chiyoda is perfectly located for this). Visit Kitanomaru Park and the Budokan area one last time. Pick up any final souvenirs at the KITTE shopping complex next to Tokyo Station (excellent Japanese craft and food selections).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — last-minute shopping at Tokyo Station's Gransta and First Avenue underground malls (best selection of omiyage/souvenir foods in Tokyo). Pack carefully, check out of hotel, and head to the airport with ample time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — transfer to airport. Narita Express from Tokyo Station takes ~60 min. Haneda Airport is ~30 min by monorail or Keikyu Line.

meals.breakfast: Final Tokyo breakfast — a proper Japanese breakfast set (gohan, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, tamagoyaki) at a restaurant near the Imperial Palace (~¥1,000-1,500)
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station ekiben (train station bento box) — a uniquely Japanese tradition. Choose from dozens of regional bento boxes at the Gransta market for a delicious farewell meal (~¥1,200-1,800)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in, immigration, and security. Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ¥220 handling fee) or keep it for future Japan trips — it never expires. Pack any liquid food souvenirs (soy sauce, sake) in checked luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Arrive early to catch the freshest produce and interact with vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a hefty price tag. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 morning to kick off your culinary journey refreshed.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in: Flight lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay via private luxury car service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Imperial Palace East Gardens Stroll: Just minutes from the hotel, explore the serene East Gardens of the Imperial Palace. Walk the manicured grounds, admire the ancient stone walls, and enjoy the spring cherry blossom remnants in a tranquil, crowd-light setting.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner at Kanda Yabu Soba or Sushi Yoshitake (Ginza, 3-Michelin-star): Ease into Tokyo's culinary world with an intimate omakase sushi dinner. Let the chef guide you through seasonal nigiri crafted with the finest Toyosu Market fish.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome amenity at hotel or casual ramen at a nearby Chiyoda noodle shop upon arrival
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at Sushi Yoshitake, Ginza — expect 18–20 courses of seasonal nigiri, approx. ¥55,000–¥70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Confirm Michelin restaurant reservation at least 2–3 months ahead. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour: Join a guided premium food tour of the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample ultra-fresh sushi, house-made tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, wagyu skewers, and artisan pickles. Learn the history of Tokyo's legendary fish trade from a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay Cruise: Walk to the adjacent Hamarikyu Gardens, a stunning feudal-era landscape garden with a tidal pond. Board a traditional yakatabune (roofed pleasure boat) for a private Tokyo Bay cruise, sipping matcha and taking in the skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Saito (Kaiseki, Minato): Experience a multi-course kaiseki dinner showcasing the finest seasonal Japanese ingredients — bamboo shoots, sakura sea bream, and spring mountain vegetables — in an intimate, minimalist setting.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi and tamagoyaki at Tsukiji Outer Market as part of the food tour
meals.lunch: Continued tastings at Tsukiji — premium tuna donburi at Tsukiji Tamasushi
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Saito, Minato — approx. ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji tour should start around 08:00 for the freshest experience. Wear comfortable shoes. Hamarikyu Gardens entry ¥300. Private yakatabune cruise should be booked in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech & Culture Deep Dive: Head to Akihabara, Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop-culture district. Visit Yodobashi Camera's flagship multi-floor store, explore cutting-edge robotics and gadget shops, and discover the intersection of tech and otaku culture in dedicated concept stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Borderless (Odaiba or current venue): Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab digital art museum — a groundbreaking fusion of technology, art, and nature. Wander through luminous interactive installations that respond to your presence in real time.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Cocktails & Dinner in Roppongi: Pre-dinner cocktails at the Park Hyatt New York Bar (or Andaz Rooftop), followed by dinner at Ryugin (3-Michelin-star) — one of Tokyo's most celebrated contemporary Japanese restaurants.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a traditional Japanese breakfast set with grilled fish, miso soup, and rice
meals.lunch: Akihabara curry at a retro café, or a quick bento from a high-end depachika (department store basement food hall)
meals.dinner: Ryugin, Roppongi — innovative kaiseki, approx. ¥50,000–¥65,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be booked online well in advance — slots sell out quickly. Akihabara is best explored on foot; allow 3 hours minimum. Ryugin reservation required months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka Historic District Walking Tour: Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved shitamachi (old town) neighborhoods. Stroll through the atmospheric cemetery, browse artisan craft shops, and visit the charming Yanaka Ginza shopping street for local snacks and handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo National Museum (Ueno): Visit Japan's largest and most prestigious museum, home to an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist sculptures. Arrange a private curator-led tour for exclusive access and context.
day_by_day.evening: Ueno Izakaya Experience: Enjoy a curated private izakaya dinner in Ueno featuring premium yakitori, seasonal sashimi, house-aged sake, and regional craft beers — a convivial, authentic Tokyo evening.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and freshly baked melon pan at a Yanaka café
meals.lunch: Traditional soba lunch at a century-old Yanaka soba shop
meals.dinner: Private izakaya dinner in Ueno — curated premium course, approx. ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Book a private curator tour through the hotel concierge. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable walking shoes. Spring mornings here are especially atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Harajuku: Begin with a contemplative morning walk through the forested path of Meiji Jingu Shrine, one of Tokyo's most sacred Shinto sites. Witness traditional rituals and enjoy the peaceful cedar woodland setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Omotesando Architecture & Luxury Shopping: Stroll Tokyo's most elegant boulevard, admiring the flagship boutiques designed by Tadao Ando, Toyo Ito, and Herzog & de Meuron. Visit Omotesando Hills for curated Japanese designer labels, and explore the hidden Ura-Harajuku lanes for avant-garde fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège (Aoyama, 2-Michelin-star): Experience one of Tokyo's most exciting contemporary French-Japanese restaurants. Chef Hiroyasu Kawate's open-kitchen counter delivers theatrical, ingredient-driven cuisine with a strong sustainability ethos.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and pastry near Harajuku station
meals.lunch: Lunch at Anniversaire Café on Omotesando — elegant French-inspired bistro with terrace seating
meals.dinner: Florilège, Aoyama — contemporary French-Japanese, approx. ¥35,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Arrive before 09:00 for a quiet, crowd-free experience. Omotesando shops open around 11:00. Florilège reservation required well in advance — counter seating is the premium choice.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Crossing & Scramble Experience: Visit the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak morning hour. Observe from the Starbucks or Mag's Park vantage point, then descend into the organized chaos below. Explore Shibuya Stream and the surrounding tech-forward retail landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: CyberAgent / Digital Culture Immersion in Shibuya: Visit the Shibuya QWS innovation hub, explore the KDDI Toranomon Hills tech showroom, and browse Shibuya's cutting-edge concept stores. Arrange a private tech culture walking tour with a local guide specializing in Tokyo's startup and digital scene.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa (Minami-Aoyama, 2-Michelin-star): Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa's legendary 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' blends French technique with Japan's ancient relationship with nature. One of Asia's most celebrated dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel or artisan coffee bar near Chiyoda — try a Japanese-style morning set (tamago sando, miso soup, coffee)
meals.lunch: Shibuya Hikarie ShinQs depachika — curate your own premium bento experience from Japan's finest food producers
meals.dinner: Narisawa, Minami-Aoyama — approx. ¥50,000–¥70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Crossing is busiest at morning and evening rush hours (08:00–09:00, 17:00–19:00). Narisawa reservation essential — book 2–3 months ahead. Tech culture tour can be arranged through the hotel or a specialist Tokyo guide service.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko (Private Car): Depart early by private luxury car to Nikko, UNESCO World Heritage site. Explore the spectacular Tosho-gu Shrine complex — a baroque masterpiece of gilded wood carvings, lacquerwork, and towering cedar forests dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nikko Continued — Kegon Falls & Lake Chuzenji: Drive up the winding Irohazaka road to Lake Chuzenji and witness the thundering 97-meter Kegon Waterfall. Enjoy the mountain scenery and fresh alpine air before returning to Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo & Relaxed Dinner in Ginza: After the day trip, enjoy a refined but relaxed dinner at Ginza Kojyu (4-Michelin-star kaiseki) or opt for a premium sushi counter at Harutaka for a more intimate wind-down experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at Nikko's renowned Gyoshintei restaurant, set within a historic garden
meals.dinner: Harutaka, Ginza — premium nigiri omakase, approx. ¥40,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Private car to Nikko takes approx. 2 hours each way. Depart by 07:30 to maximize time. Nikko can be cold — bring a light jacket. Tosho-gu entry fee approx. ¥1,300. Book Gyoshintei lunch in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Kagurazaka French-Japanese Quarter: Explore Kagurazaka, Tokyo's most Parisian neighborhood. Wander the narrow cobblestone alleys (yokocho), discover hidden French bistros, traditional ryotei, and artisan shops. Visit the Zenkokuji Temple and the charming Bishamonten Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cooking Class with a Michelin-Starred Chef: Participate in a private hands-on Japanese cooking class led by a Michelin-recognized chef. Learn to prepare dashi stock, seasonal miso soup, sushi rice, and a signature dish — an immersive cultural and culinary experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Quintessence (Shirokanedai, 3-Michelin-star): Chef Kishida's French cuisine is one of Tokyo's most refined and consistent. The tasting menu showcases extraordinary technique and the finest French and Japanese produce.

meals.breakfast: Artisan bakery breakfast in Kagurazaka — La Boulangerie Inatani or similar
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during your cooking class, enjoyed with sake or green tea
meals.dinner: Quintessence, Shirokanedai — approx. ¥45,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Private cooking classes can be arranged through the hotel or services like Cookly or Airbnb Experiences (premium tier). Quintessence reservation required far in advance. Kagurazaka is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba & Future City Exploration: Take the Yurikamome monorail across the Rainbow Bridge to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) — home to ASIMO robots, interactive AI exhibits, and a stunning geodesic globe displaying real-time Earth data.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Planets (Toyosu) — if not visited earlier: Immerse yourself in this separate teamLab installation focused on water, flowers, and bodily immersion. Alternatively, explore the Toyota Mega Web showroom or the Panasonic Center Tokyo for cutting-edge consumer tech.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a Sumida River Yakatabune: Board a private luxury yakatabune (traditional wooden pleasure boat) for a multi-course dinner cruise along the Sumida River. Drift past illuminated bridges and the Tokyo Skytree while enjoying seasonal Japanese cuisine and sake.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ramen at a premium Odaiba ramen restaurant, or sushi at the Odaiba Aqua City food floor
meals.dinner: Private yakatabune dinner cruise — approx. ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person, bookable through specialist operators

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. Book yakatabune dinner cruise at least 1–2 weeks in advance through the hotel concierge. teamLab Planets requires advance online booking. Bring comfortable footwear for the monorail and walking.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa & Senso-ji Temple: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple, Senso-ji in Asakusa. Arrive early to experience the incense-laden atmosphere before the crowds. Explore Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki sweets, and handmade tenugui textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sumida — Craft Sake & Whisky Tasting: Visit the Sumida River Brewing Company for a craft beer tasting, then join a private whisky tasting session at a specialist bar featuring rare Japanese single malts from Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Nikka. Learn from a certified whisky sommelier.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (if accessible) or Sushi Sho: Experience one of Tokyo's most legendary and exclusive sushi counters. Sushi Saito is considered by many to be the finest sushi restaurant in the world — reservations require a local contact or hotel concierge connection.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a historic Asakusa ryokan café — try dashimaki tamago and grilled fish
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa — a 130-year-old institution serving crispy sesame-oil tempura
meals.dinner: Sushi Saito or Sushi Sho — approx. ¥60,000–¥80,000 per person (if accessible)

day_by_day.notes: Sushi Saito reservations are notoriously difficult — the hotel concierge at a top Tokyo property is your best asset. Senso-ji is open 24 hours; the main hall opens at 06:00. Whisky tasting can be arranged through Bar Benfiddich or a specialist tasting service.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku — Kabukicho & Golden Gai Exploration (Daytime): Explore Shinjuku in the daylight — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for panoramic views from the free observation deck. Walk through the serene Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Japan's finest landscape parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Samurai & Ninja Museum / Traditional Arts: Visit the Samurai Museum in Shinjuku for an immersive experience with authentic armor, swords, and theatrical samurai demonstrations. Alternatively, attend a private tea ceremony at Urasenke or Omotesenke — one of Japan's most prestigious tea schools.
day_by_day.evening: Golden Gai Bar Crawl & Dinner: As night falls, explore the legendary Golden Gai — a labyrinth of 200+ tiny bars, each with its own character. Begin with cocktails at a curated selection of Golden Gai bars, then enjoy dinner at Kozue (Park Hyatt Tokyo) — stunning Japanese cuisine with panoramic Shinjuku views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Shinjuku depachika morning pastry and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Shinjuku Gyoen — premium bento from Isetan's basement food hall
meals.dinner: Kozue, Park Hyatt Tokyo — Japanese haute cuisine with city views, approx. ¥30,000–¥45,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry ¥500. Private tea ceremony requires advance booking. Golden Gai bars are cash-only and have a cover charge (¥500–¥1,000). Kozue reservation recommended. Shinjuku is easily reached from Chiyoda by subway.

day_by_day.morning: Daikanyama & Nakameguro Lifestyle District: Explore Daikanyama, Tokyo's most stylish residential neighborhood. Visit the iconic Tsutaya Books (Daikanyama T-Site) — a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural hub. Browse curated concept stores, design galleries, and artisan coffee shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nakameguro Canal Walk & Art Galleries: Stroll along the picturesque Meguro River canal, lined with boutique restaurants, independent galleries, and design studios. Visit a contemporary art gallery in the area and explore the creative energy of this beloved Tokyo neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Yebisu Garden Place, 3-Michelin-star): Celebrate your final full evening with dinner at one of Tokyo's most opulent restaurants. The grand Louis XVI-inspired dining room and Robuchon's legendary cuisine — including the iconic pomme purée — create an unforgettable finale.

meals.breakfast: Specialty coffee and avocado toast or Japanese-French fusion breakfast at Daikanyama Log Road café
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nakameguro's Log Road dining terrace or a stylish Italian trattoria along the canal
meals.dinner: Joël Robuchon Tokyo, Yebisu — grand French tasting menu, approx. ¥60,000–¥85,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsutaya Books Daikanyama opens at 07:00 — a magical early morning visit. Joël Robuchon reservation essential. The restaurant has a formal dress code — jacket required. Yebisu Garden Place is a 10-minute taxi from Nakameguro.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Chiyoda — Kitanomaru Park & Budokan: Take a peaceful morning walk through Kitanomaru Park, adjacent to the Imperial Palace. Visit the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) if open, or simply enjoy a quiet farewell stroll along the palace moat as the city awakens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-Minute Luxury Shopping & Depachika: Head to Ginza for final luxury shopping — visit the Ginza Six rooftop garden, browse Itoya stationery, and descend into the Mitsukoshi or Matsuya basement food halls for premium Japanese confections, wagashi, and gourmet gifts to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure: Private luxury transfer to airport. Arrive with ample time for premium lounge access before your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor a full traditional Japanese set one last time
meals.lunch: Ginza Six or Mitsukoshi depachika — create a curated farewell meal from Japan's finest artisan food producers
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or early dinner at Ginza before transfer — try Ginza Kyubey for a final sushi experience

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Private car transfer should be booked the day before. Duty-free shopping at Narita or Haneda is excellent — budget time for it. Pack wagashi, matcha, and sake gifts carefully to comply with customs regulations.
